name: Kingdom of Kush
summary: A Nubian kingdom on the Nile that conquered Egypt as its 25th Dynasty, then ruled from Meroë, where it built more pyramids than Egypt.

location.value: The Nile Valley in what is now northern Sudan and southern Egypt.

terrain.value: The Nile valley with its cataracts (rapids), surrounded by desert and, further south, savannah.

climate.value: Hot desert in the north; summer rains around Meroë.

resources.value: Gold, iron, ivory, ebony and incense.
resources.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Kush (checked 6 Nov 2026); Edwards, The Nubian Past (2004)

population.value: About 1,150,000 in the Meroitic phase (Wikipedia infobox).

urbanisation.value: Capitals at Napata and Meroë, with temples, palaces and royal pyramids.

migration.value: Movement of Noba and Blemmyes peoples late in the kingdom’s life.

economicBase.value: A complex economy based on trade and industry, farming and herding.

tradeRoutes.value: Trade with Egypt and the Mediterranean in gold, ivory and other goods.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.

moneyAndTax.value: No coinage of its own; exchange in goods.

inequality.value: Royal and priestly elites held great wealth.

governmentType.value: Monarchy, with powerful queens (kandakes) who sometimes ruled alone.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Kush (checked 6 Nov 2026); Edwards, The Nubian Past (2004)

keyRulers.value: Kashta, Piye (founder of Egypt’s 25th Dynasty), Taharqa, Amanirenas.

succession.value: Hereditary, with an important role for the queen mother.

institutions.value: Temples of Amun played a key role in choosing and crowning kings.

stability.value: Lost Egypt to Assyria in the 7th century BCE.

armyAndTech.value: Kushites were famous archers; Egyptians called Nubia “the land of the bow”.
armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Kush (checked 6 Nov 2026); Edwards, The Nubian Past (2004)

majorWars.value: Wars with Assyria; queen Amanirenas fought Rome (c. 25–22 BCE).

territoryChange.value: Ruled Egypt as the 25th Dynasty, then lost it to Assyria.

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals: Egypt, Assyria, Rome and finally Aksum.
alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Kush (checked 6 Nov 2026); Edwards, The Nubian Past (2004)

scienceEducation.value: Meroitic script, a writing system of its own.

openness.value: Combined Egyptian religion and art with local traditions.

religion.value: Kushite and Egyptian religion, especially worship of Amun.

languageWriting.value: Meroitic, Egyptian and Old Nubian; Meroitic script is not fully understood.

artsArchitecture.value: The Nubian pyramids of Meroë and the temple of Jebel Barkal.
artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Kush (checked 6 Nov 2026); Edwards, The Nubian Past (2004)

socialStructure.value: Unusually high levels of women’s participation, including ruling queens.

sharedIdentity.value: Kushite kingship and the worship of Amun.

neighbours.value: Egypt, Assyria, Rome, Aksum and peoples of the Sahara.
neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Kush (checked 6 Nov 2026); Edwards, The Nubian Past (2004)

ideasReligions.value: Egyptian religion spread south along the Nile.

colonisation.value: Egypt’s New Kingdom had annexed Kush before the kingdom formed.

riseSignals.value: The kings of Napata grew strong enough to conquer Egypt.

peakPeriod.value: The 25th Dynasty ruled Egypt and Kush together.

declineSignals.value: Loss of trade, pressure from Noba, Blemmyes and Aksum.

outcome.value: Disintegrated in the 4th century CE into Nobatia, Makuria and Alodia.

sources.value: Archaeology at Meroë and Napata, Egyptian and Greek sources. Checked against Wikipedia (“Kingdom of Kush”).

overallCertainty.value: Medium. Its start date and the Meroitic script are uncertain. Second source: Wikidata includes the earlier Kerma kingdom (from c. 2180 BCE); this app starts with Napatan Kush (c. 780 BCE).

knownFor.label: Pyramids of Meroë
knownFor.note: Steep pyramids built for Kushite kings and queens.

knownFor.label: Kushite archers
knownFor.note: Egyptians called Nubia “the land of the bow”.

knownFor.label: Iron smelting at Meroë
knownFor.note: Large slag heaps show a big iron industry.
